Background (from the session that started this one):
JusPrin 2 is a desktop 3D-printing slicer (a fork of OrcaSlicer, C++ with wxWidgets and two React pages; repository `/Users/kenneth/Projects/JusPrin`, public on GitHub) with its own server in the private tsd-enterprise repository. In November 2026 Kenneth set rules for error handling. A condition we can name in advance and that the person can act on is an expected error: it is designed when the feature is built and gets a sentence he approved. Everything else is a surprise: no handling is written for it, it stops the work, and it is reported to Sentry with everything known. On 2026-11-20 he added that the log must capture every failure, expected or unexpected, and that a log line never stands in for a report. That request reached this session through another session Kenneth was talking to, which relayed his words: "tell the main session to create a task chip to do so." The app reports through `report_unexpected_error` and `report_if_automatic` (`Support/ErrorReport.hpp`), sent by Sentry's native SDK (`Support/SentryClient.cpp`); the server reports through Sentry's Django integration and the gateway's own top handler. On the server, Sentry is set up so that no log line becomes a Sentry event, so logging and reporting are separate there. Kenneth wants reports in plain language: full sentences, no made-up labels, decisions asked as full "Decision needed" paragraphs, and inference marked as inference.

Task:
Check the JusPrin desktop app and the JusPrin 2 server against the logging rule, and fix the places that miss it.

**The rule.** Kenneth's words: "also make sure the log captures everything. expected, or unexpected." It is written in the "Error handling" rules as: "Every failure is written to the log, expected or unexpected. The log is kept as well as the report, never in its place." Read the whole "Error handling" section first: in `AGENTS.md` of `/Users/kenneth/Projects/JusPrin` (on `jusprin-dev`, commit `e109da5c29` or later, under "Two kinds of failure"), and in `CLAUDE.md` of tsd-enterprise. The server's copy of the new text was still uncommitted when this was written, in `/Users/kenneth/Projects/tsd-enterprise/.claude/worktrees/error-lesson-docs/CLAUDE.md`; read it there if `master` does not have it yet.

**The task.**
1. In the app (`src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/` and its two pages, `AgentUI` and `HomeUI`) and the server (`web_ent/jusprin/` in `/Users/kenneth/Projects/tsd-enterprise`), find every place the code decides that something failed. That means both kinds: an expected error that gets a sentence or a named answer, and an unexpected one that is thrown and reported.
2. For each, check that a log line is written with what the code knew at that point: what it was doing, the other side's status, request id and error text, and the request's own facts.
3. Fix the ones that write nothing. Prefer one line at the place that already handles the failure (the top handler for unexpected errors; the function that builds an expected answer) over a line at every site.

Nobody has checked this yet. An earlier trace looked only at what reaches Sentry. Two things it noticed in passing, to verify and not to take as the whole list: the server gateway's top handler (`web_ent/jusprin/v2/gateway.py`, about line 139) reports to Sentry and writes no log line; and in the app an expected answer to a failed AI request (`http_error` and `provider_answer` in `Agent/ProviderAgent.cpp`) appears to return its sentence without logging.

**Two conflicts to put to Kenneth, not to settle yourself.** Ask each as a full "Decision needed" paragraph with the options and what each costs, and carry on with the rest meanwhile.
- `error_body()` in `web_ent/jusprin/v2/errors.py` logs an expected answer's code only, on purpose, because the message and details can hold a person's credit numbers. "Captures everything" would change that.
- The app attaches the run's log file to every error report and crash it sends to Sentry (`Support/SentryClient.cpp`). The report dialog promises what a report does not contain (no chat messages, no project names). A fuller log may break that promise. Read the dialog's text (`Shell/ErrorReportDialog.cpp`) and say what a new log line would add to a report.

**How to work.**
- Show it, do not only read it: for a few failures of each kind, make the failure happen in a scratch copy of the app (its own data folder; never Kenneth's running JusPrin) or on the one local server stack, and show the log before and after your change.
- Send nothing to a real Sentry project.
- JusPrin: a new branch from `jusprin-dev` in a worktree under `/Users/kenneth/Projects/JusPrin/.claude/worktrees/`; never check `jusprin-dev` out in a worktree. tsd-enterprise: other sessions share that checkout, and when this was written it held another session's uncommitted changes to `web_ent/jusprin/v2/gateway.py` and `errors.py`. Check `git status` there first; if those are still uncommitted, tell Kenneth before you edit the same files. Never stage `obico-server` or `.claude/launch.json`.
- Commit only when Kenneth asks, push only when he asks, no attribution lines. Builds on this Mac are shared: check `uptime` and `pgrep -fl ninja`, build with `-- -j4`.

**Done looks like:** a list of every place a failure is decided, each marked "logged" or "was not logged, now is", with file and line; the before-and-after log lines for the ones you made happen; the tests you ran; and Kenneth's answers to the two questions, or a note that they are still open. ## Error handling

Less is more. An error is **expected** only when the person can do something about it, such as sign in again, get more credits, update a key or check the network, and Kenneth decided what the product tells them. Every other error is **unexpected**: the person sees one generic sentence and a way to report the problem, and the report carries everything known, so that we can find the cause.

Kenneth, 2026-11-16: "if the error is something that user can do nothing about, just show the user a generic error message and give user a way to report a problem. On the back end though, we need to make sure we send as much info as possible to the Sentry server so that we can do root cause analysis. And that's it, nothing else." And: "When it comes to error handling, less is more."

The reporting function is `report_unexpected_error` (`src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/Support/ErrorReport.hpp`). This repository has no expected-errors table yet.

### Two kinds of failure

A condition we can name in advance, and that the person can act on, is an expected error. It is designed for when the feature is built, like any other part of the feature, once we have verified how it shows up: from the other side's documentation or a real answer, not from memory.

Everything else is a surprise, an unexpected error. No handling is written for it, it stops the work, and it is reported with everything known. The reporting must be complete, because a surprise that is not reported is lost. A failure that ends in a log line alone, a default value, or a sentence for "anything else" is a hole. Reading the code can check this: from each place work starts, follow a failure up to the handler that reports it.

Reports then show which surprises to fix, and which are really conditions that need a design.

Every failure is written to the log, expected or unexpected. The log is kept as well as the report, never in its place.

### Expected errors

- Each has an entry in the expected-errors table: the cause, what the person sees, and what they can do next. A new entry needs Kenneth's yes; quote his words in the commit message.
- The test is what the person can do next. If the answer is "nothing" or only "try again later", the error is unexpected. An AI provider or our own server being slow, overloaded, down or limiting us is unexpected: the person can do nothing about any of them.
- Two causes that leave the person doing the same thing do not get separate sentences, codes or branches.
- A cause is "out of credits" or "no network". A status code, an exception type, or "the request was not valid" is not a cause.
- Each entry has a test, and each occurrence is counted.
- Handle them with normal control flow, not exceptions.

### Unexpected errors

- Write no code for them. Do not catch one, give it a default value, retry it, or give it a sentence of its own. Each of those is a guess about a failure nobody understands. It hides the failure and loses where it came from.

A JusPrin git worktree builds against the already-built deps by configuring:

```
cmake -B build/arm64 -G "Ninja Multi-Config" -DCMAKE_BUILD_TYPE=Release \
  -DCMAKE_OSX_ARCHITECTURES=arm64 -DCMAKE_OSX_DEPLOYMENT_TARGET=15.0 \
  -DCMAKE_PREFIX_PATH=/Users/kenneth/Projects/JusPrin/deps/build/arm64/OrcaSlicer_dep/usr/local \
  -DSLIC3R_GUI=ON -DSLIC3R_STATIC=ON -DSLIC3R_PCH=ON -DBUILD_TESTS=ON \
  -DCMAKE_AR=/opt/homebrew/opt/llvm/bin/llvm-ar -DCMAKE_RANLIB=/opt/homebrew/opt/llvm/bin/llvm-ranlib
```

ONE PREFIX PATH (2026-11-15): since the 2.5.0 merge, CMakeLists.txt finds its bundled Python under CMAKE_PREFIX_PATH + /libpython; a two-entry list fails configure with "Bundled Python executable not found under <a;b>/libpython/bin". Pass only the JusPrin deps path (as other worktrees' caches do).

CMAKE BINARY (2026-09-29): configure with `/Applications/CMake.app/Contents/bin/cmake` (put it first on PATH). Homebrew's cmake 4.1 at /opt/homebrew/bin fails with "Could NOT find Eigen3 (missing: EIGEN3_VERSION_OK) (Required is at least version 5.0.1)", and a failed configure poisons the cache: `rm -rf build` before retrying.

The two `CMAKE_AR`/`CMAKE_RANLIB` flags are required on a FRESH build dir:
without them Apple's ar is used and liblibslic3r_gui.a (>4 GiB in
RelWithDebInfo) fails to archive. They only work at first configure, not on
reconfigure. Full story: agent-docs/macos-build-troubleshooting.md. See
[[liblibslic3r-gui-4gib-ar-limit]].

FRESH WORKTREE TRAP (2026-09-18): building only `shell_integration_harness`
does not build the web pages. Also build `--target jusprin_web jusprin_catalogs`
(needs node on PATH: /Users/kenneth/.nvm/versions/node/v24.13.0/bin). Without
them resources/jusprin/{home,agent}/index.html are missing, no web views are
created, and the harness silently tests something else (printer panel starts
shown; web-view crashes vanish).

`BUILD_TESTS=ON` is required or the tests/ tree (workspace, shell targets) is
not generated. Build with `cmake --build build/arm64 --config RelWithDebInfo
--target <targets>`. wxWidgets 3.3 sources for API verification live under
/Users/kenneth/Projects/OrcaSlicer/deps/build/arm64/dep_wxWidgets-prefix/.

CWD TRAP (cost real time once): the harness resets the Bash cwd to the main
repo /Users/kenneth/Projects/JusPrin between turns, so a *relative*
`cmake --build build/arm64` silently builds the MAIN repo's build dir, not the
worktree's — the worktree binary then runs stale code and a re-fix looks like it
"didn't take". Always pass the worktree build dir as an ABSOLUTE path to
`cmake --build /…/.claude/worktrees/<wt>/build/arm64 …`, and run test binaries by
absolute path. Also: `cmake --build --target <one_exe>` may relink against a
stale lib without recompiling a changed .cpp in that lib — build the app target
(e.g. OrcaSlicer) too so the lib recompiles; verify with
`grep -c '<file>.cpp.o' build.log`. Editing tools (Edit/Write) use absolute
paths so source edits land correctly regardless of cwd.

STALE PROMPT TRAP (2026-09-23): `--target shell_integration_harness` does NOT
rebuild the web pages, so a harness run after an edit to AgentUI (for example
printerInstructions.ts) loads the old bundle. Six --printer-live runs were
wasted this way. After any page edit, build `jusprin_web` explicitly and check
the new text is in resources/jusprin/agent/index.html before running live.

DISK (2026-10-10): building with `--config Release` instead of RelWithDebInfo made a fresh worktree build dir 859 MB instead of ~14 GB, needed no llvm-ar relink, and the shell harness ran normally from `tests/shell/Release/`. Use it when the disk is nearly full (it was at 99%) and no debugger is needed. With other sessions building, a fresh build took far longer than usual (machine load 30 to 85).

On 2026-10-28 I walked six scenarios (open-and-print, fix-a-problem) through the real app with Opus 5.5 and published the critique at https://claude.ai/artifact/XyVvteGiKhiJ6apUx8rcmR (34 frames, scratch copy at scratchpad/ux/ of that session). Kenneth's steer: start from files people actually download (MakerWorld 3MFs carry a full Bambu profile: printer, print preset, filaments, colours, bed type, designer, licence), not from generated STLs. `~/Downloads` has Tape_4_3MF.3mf (A1 mini profile), find_my_hollow.3mf (P1S, 3 colours, 233 mm wide, too big for an A1 mini), arrow_headband.3mf (P1S), general_purpose_hook.STL (bare).

**Recipe that worked**
- `ditto` the built .app out of `build/arm64/src/RelWithDebInfo/` into the scratchpad before launching (another session's ninja can relink it underneath you); the bundle id is already unique (`io.jusprin.JusPrin`), no re-sign needed.
- `ditto` `~/Library/Application Support/JusPrin2` to a scratch `--datadir`; set `jusprin.fake_printer=true`, `presets.machine` to the saved "Bambu Lab A1 mini 2", write `jusprin/fake_printer.json`, delete `jusprin/mcp.json.lock`.
- **Clear `local_machines`.** Kenneth's conf carries a `local_machines` entry keyed by the empty string (old Moonraker experiment). With the fake Bambu agent on, `init_networking_callbacks`' connect callback calls `DeviceManager::set_selected_machine("")` in a loop ("same lan machine, dev_id =, disconnect and reconnect"), the main window disappears and the log grew 700 MB in two minutes. Clearing the map fixed it. The loop has no guard; see [[fake-bambu-printer-sim]] and [[harness-fake-printer-cleanup]].
- Background `app_*` tools cannot press OrcaSlicer's custom `Button`s (no AX action) and the hit test at the dialog's screen position reports "belongs to a different process". `request_full_control` + `computer_batch` works for everything, including the Agent web view and the macOS file chooser (`cmd+shift+g`, type the path, Return, Return). Re-front the app with `open_application` when another session's harness steals focus.
- Every `app_screenshot`/`computer_batch` screenshot is written as a JPEG under `~/.claude/projects/<project>/<session>/tool-results/mcp-computer-use-blob-*.jpg`; copy those for a report instead of fighting `screencapture`.
- The dev build (-O0) slices a 38 mm part in over a minute; wait 45–60 s before judging a slice.

**Why:** the first launch attempt looked like an app bug (blank window, title "Couldn't save") and cost ten minutes; the dialog-click refusals cost another ten.
**How to apply:** reuse this for any "walk through the app as a user" request; keep scenarios on downloaded files; write the critique per step as what the person knows / sees / finds confusing. Related: [[live-test-built-app-on-mac]], [[drive-app-with-posted-key-events]].
